newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian OTC stocks trade erodes in week to May 29.
newsitem.headline: Croatian OTC stocks trade erodes in week to May 29.

text.p: The Croatian over-the-counter stocks trade eroded further in the shorter week to May 29, ahead of the Statehood Day public holiday, the Varazdin market reported on Friday.
Volume fell to 7,381 units, of which 1,101 were sold in direct deals and only reported by brokers. Turnover was almost halved at 1.8 million kuna.
The leading seven-stock VIN index eased another 0.15 percent to 9,603 points as 15 traded issues fell, four rose and four remained unchanged from a week earlier.
Hoteli Njivice made a debut, selling 105 shares at 140 kuna each.

Ericsson Nikola Tesla, a subsidiary of Sweden's electronic giant, was again the most active issue with a total of 1,728 shares. It closed 20 percent higher at 180 kuna after trading in a 155-195 kuna range.
Gainers were led by the Rijeka repair docks Viktor Lenac, rising 36.22 percent to 267 kuna on volume of 100 shares.
Distillery Badel 1862 had the biggest dip of 37.11 percent to 100 kuna with 170 shares changing hands.

Food processor Podravka closed at 245 kuna after a new 5.77-percent loss on volume of 441 shares. It seemed to reverse its recent downslide on the central bourse in Zagreb, ending five kuna higher at 260 on Thursday.
Another popular stock, chocolate maker Kras, inched down 0.73 percent on a weekly basis to 407 kuna, three down from its close on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
